acceptance: A table of REST requests per caller for one working day is recorded on this item, with the method, and names the top three consumers.
An owner decision among options (a), (b) and (c) is recorded, with any follow-up items created and linked.
Each of the seven symptom items is either linked from here as still needed, or dropped as merged into another with its unique evidence moved first.
If option (a) is chosen, the expected saving per day is stated from the measurement, so the follow-up can be checked against it.
description:
Between 2026-11-12 and 2026-11-13 separate sessions filed at least seven items for what looks like one cause: several concurrent agent sessions use the same GitHub user (5,000 REST requests per hour, exhausted twice within an hour on 2026-11-12) and the same loaded host, and the tools they call treat a transient failure as final.
- pr-arm-github-rate-limit-backoff-20261112 and pr-open-and-pr-arm-fail-on-github-rate-limit-20261112: landing targets exit on a rate limit.
- branch-prune-merged-exhausts-github-quota-20261112: one target spends a request per branch.
- review-verdict-prepare-fails-on-transient-503-20261112 and theseus-gate-transient-github-timeout-20261113: hosted review jobs fail on one 503 or timeout.
- tractable-mcp-request-timeouts-20261112 and tractable-mcp-write-timeout-unknown-outcome-20261113: tracker writes outlast the client timeout under load.
Each item fixes one symptom. None measures who spends the quota, sets a budget, or decides whether sessions should stop sharing one identity. Three duplicates were filed in two days, which is itself a cost of having no owner.

This item is the analysis and the decision, not the fixes. It ends with a recorded decision and links; the symptom items stay where they are.

Decision gates.
- Measure before proposing: one working day of REST use per caller (make target or script), taken from `gh api rate_limit` samples and the callers' own logs. `gh api rate_limit` does not count against the quota.
- Then choose, with the owner: (a) cut calls in the top consumers (conditional requests, GraphQL for batched reads, fewer polls); (b) give agent sessions a separate identity or a GitHub App installation token with its own quota; (c) accept the limit and rely on the backoff items. Option (b) changes credentials and identity, which is owner-only: propose it, do not do it.
- Decide whether the duplicates should be merged into fewer items once the cause is confirmed.

Guardrails.
- No credential, token, App or secret is created, rotated or stored under this item, and none is written to Git, logs or the tracker.
- Commit identity rules are unchanged: a separate API identity must never become a commit author.
- Measurement must not itself spend meaningful quota or add writes to the tracker store.
- No check is skipped or made non-blocking to save requests.
